articles.title: REPAIR Act Gains Momentum with 12 New House Cosponsors
articles.summary: The Right to Equitable and Professional Auto Industry Repair Act has added 12 new cosponsors, bringing the total to 67 as the bill sits in House Energy and Commerce Committee.

briefing.impact: More cosponsors signals growing bipartisan support — this bill is alive and moving despite manufacturer opposition.
briefing.timeline: Committee hearing expected Q2–Q3 2026 if momentum holds.
briefing.action: Contact your representative and ask them to cosponsor H.R. 906.

articles.title: Texas Lane Filtering Bill Passes House Transportation Committee
articles.summary: Texas HB 1927 passed the House Transportation Committee 8–3 and heads to a full House floor vote, potentially making Texas the largest state to permit motorcycle lane filtering.

briefing.impact: Texas passing lane filtering would accelerate adoption nationally — the state's size gives it outsized influence on transportation policy.
briefing.timeline: Full House vote expected within 3–4 weeks of session calendar.
briefing.action: If you ride in Texas, contact your state rep to support HB 1927.

articles.title: AMA Releases 2026 State Legislative Watchlist
articles.summary: The AMA is tracking 34 active state bills in the 2026 session covering lane filtering, helmet choice, right to repair, and motorcycle profiling — the largest legislative watchlist in five years.

briefing.impact: More active bills means more chances for wins — and more threats. Rider engagement at the state level has never mattered more.
briefing.timeline: Most state sessions run through June or July 2026.
briefing.action: Visit amacycle.org/action to find your state's active bills.

articles.title: Ohio Riders Push to Repeal 1978 Helmet Mandate
articles.summary: Ohio HB 244 would repeal universal helmet coverage for riders 21 and older who carry adequate insurance, restoring adult choice. The bill is before the House Transportation Committee.

briefing.impact: Ohio would join Michigan and several other states in granting adult riders the choice — a significant shift in a traditionally conservative-law state.
briefing.timeline: Committee vote not yet scheduled. ABATE Ohio is lobbying actively.
briefing.action: Ohio riders: contact your state rep. Find the bill at legislature.ohio.gov.

articles.title: Harley-Davidson and Indian Fight REPAIR Act in Senate Testimony
articles.summary: Representatives from major powersports manufacturers testified against the REPAIR Act, arguing that shared telematics access creates cybersecurity risks and enables intellectual property theft.

briefing.impact: Manufacturer opposition is organized and well-funded — this is the main obstacle to passage. Their cybersecurity argument is the one that lands with swing-vote senators.
briefing.timeline: Senate version has not yet been introduced; House bill is the live vehicle.
briefing.action: The AMA has a rebuttal toolkit at amacycle.org — use it when contacting your senator.

articles.title: Minnesota Lane Filtering Bill Gets New Life with Safety Data
articles.summary: Minnesota HF 1623 is advancing with new backing from a University of Minnesota traffic study showing lane filtering reduces rear-end collisions involving motorcyclists by 37% in urban settings.

briefing.impact: Academic safety data is changing the argument from 'rider preference' to 'public safety' — a much stronger position with legislators.
briefing.timeline: Transportation Finance Committee vote expected in May 2026.
briefing.action: Minnesota riders: the MRF has a form letter at mrf.org for this bill.

articles.title: NHTSA Proposes Updated Helmet Safety Standards Under FMVSS 218
articles.summary: NHTSA published a proposed rulemaking to update Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 218, tightening performance requirements for DOT-certified helmets. No federal mandate is proposed.

briefing.impact: No threat to rider choice here — this is about improving the quality floor of DOT-certified helmets, not requiring everyone to wear one.
briefing.timeline: 60-day public comment period open through June 27, 2026.
briefing.action: Comment at regulations.gov if you want your voice in the record.

articles.title: Massachusetts Right to Repair Ruling: What It Means for Riders
articles.summary: A federal district court upheld Massachusetts' auto right-to-repair law, rejecting NHTSA's preemption argument. Legal experts say the ruling strengthens the case for federal legislation.

briefing.impact: This court win creates legal precedent that state right-to-repair laws can coexist with federal vehicle safety standards — a direct counter to the manufacturer lobby's main legal argument against H.R. 906.
briefing.timeline: Appeal possible through 2026; federal REPAIR Act proponents are citing this ruling in committee testimony.
briefing.action: Follow the case if you're in MA — it's the template for what federal law could do nationally.

articles.title: Motorcycle Riders Foundation Launches 'Ride the Vote' Campaign
articles.summary: The MRF is launching a voter registration and advocacy campaign targeting the 10 million registered motorcyclists in America ahead of the 2026 midterm elections.

briefing.impact: 10 million registered motorcyclists is a meaningful voting bloc in swing districts — especially in the Midwest. Politicians are paying attention.
briefing.action: Register at mrf.org and let your elected officials know riders vote on these issues.

articles.title: Lane Splitting Legal in Four States: What Riders Need to Know
articles.summary: California, Utah, Montana, and Hawaii now permit some form of lane splitting or filtering. Arizona came close this session. Here's a breakdown of current laws and what's next.

briefing.impact: The domino is falling. Each state that passes filtering makes the next one easier — legislators can point to real-world safety data instead of debating hypotheticals.
briefing.timeline: Arizona expected to revisit in 2027 session. Texas, Ohio, and Georgia are the nearest dominoes.
briefing.action: Check your state's status on this tracker and support your state AMA affiliate.
